name: Labeled Sample Compression
definition: The **Labeled Sample Compression** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the smallest $k$ for which every realizable labeled sample can be reduced to at most $k$ labeled examples from which a reconstruction function returns a hypothesis consistent with the whole sample.
graph_summary: Smallest number of labeled sample examples sufficient for consistent reconstruction.
origin_references: The standard sample-compression framework is developed in \cite{FW1995}.

monotonic.proof: Restrict a possibly improper labeled compression scheme for $\mathcal H$ to samples realizable by $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$.  Its reconstruction remains consistent, with the same compression bound.

p_monotonic.proof: Regard a labeled sample on retained coordinates as a labeled sample on the original domain, apply the scheme for $\mathcal H$, and restrict the reconstruction.  Any projected-realizable sample has an extension in $\mathcal H$, so the restricted reconstruction is consistent and uses no more retained labeled examples.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.
